# What this vignette covers

The Offender Tracking Information System (OTIS) tables, published by
the Ontario Ministry of the Solicitor General on data.ontario.ca,
describe restrictive confinement and segregation in Ontario's
provincial institutions. This vignette shows the rmorie functions that
work with them:

- where the OTIS tables come from, online and offline;
- `morie_otis_analyze_a01_mrm()`, which runs a ten-estimator causal
  ensemble on the canonical a01 design;
- `morie_mrm_estimate_causal_effect()`, the general multi-estimator
  entry point, on the same design;
- `morie_otis_irr_glmm_vm()`, the aggregate incidence-rate ratio;
- the Mandela-Rules classifiers and the federal comparison tables.

```{r setup}
library(rmorie)
```

The OTIS analysis functions return lists with a `tables` element.
This helper turns one of those tables into a data frame for printing:

```{r helper}
as_table <- function(tab) {
  rows <- lapply(tab$rows, function(r) unlist(lapply(r, as.character)))
  out <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(out) <- tab$headers
  out
}
```

# Where the OTIS data come from

The dataset catalogue lists the OTIS tables that
`morie_load_dataset()` fetches from data.ontario.ca:

```{r otis-catalog}
cat_otis <- morie_dataset_catalog()
cat_otis[cat_otis$source == "otis", c("key", "name")]
```

The full tables are downloaded on the first call and then read from
the local cache. This chunk is not run when the vignette is built: it
needs the network, and the ensemble below takes a long time on the
full a01 table (76,934 rows in October 2026; a test run had not
finished within 20 minutes):

```{r otis-download, eval = FALSE}
a01 <- morie_load_dataset("otisa01")
r_full <- morie_otis_analyze_a01_mrm(a01)
```

Offline, three kinds of OTIS data are available:

- `morie_sample("otis_b01")` is a 1,000-row extract of table b01;
  `morie_sample("otis_b09")` and `morie_sample("otis_c11")` are the
  whole b09 and c11 tables.
- `morie_otis_load()` returns the cached a01 table if there is one,
  and otherwise a 5-row synthetic sample in the a01 layout. Its
  numbers are not findings.
- `morie_synth_otis()` simulates OTIS tables with the published
  column layout. The examples below use it for the a01 design.

```{r otis-offline}
b01 <- morie_sample("otis_b01")
dim(b01)
a01_syn <- morie_synth_otis("a01", n = 300L, seed = 1L)
head(a01_syn[, c("EndFiscalYear", "UniqueIndividual_ID",
                 "MentalHealth_Alert", "SuicideRisk_Alert",
                 "SuicideWatch_Alert")], 3)
```

# The canonical a01 design

OTIS reassigns `UniqueIndividual_ID` every fiscal year, so the unit of
analysis is the person-year. For each person-year,
`morie_otis_make_pair_alert_to_volatility_ruhela()` builds:

- `ac`: the number of distinct combinations of the three alert flags
  (mental health, suicide risk, suicide watch) across that
  person-year's rows;
- the treatment `T_high_ac = 1` when `ac >= 2`;
- the outcome `Y_vm_count`: the number of region changes, counting a
  change between the region at placement and the most recent region
  within a row, and a change of region from one row to the next;
- the covariates `Gender`, `Age_Category` and `EndFiscalYear`.

```{r pair}
pair <- morie_otis_make_pair_alert_to_volatility_ruhela(a01_syn)
nrow(pair$data)
table(pair$data$T_high_ac)
```

# The ten-estimator ensemble

`morie_otis_analyze_a01_mrm()` (an alias of
`morie_otis_analyze_a01_ruhela_formulations()`) runs ten estimators on
this design: IPW (Hajek), AIPW, g-computation, 1:1 propensity-score
matching, propensity-score subclassification, IRM double machine
learning (ATE, ATTE and ATC), matching followed by IRM-DML, an AIPW
estimate of the ATC, the partially linear DML model, and a
SuperLearner-stacked AIPW. Here it runs on the simulated a01 table, so
the estimates describe the simulation, not Ontario:

```{r ensemble}
res <- morie_otis_analyze_a01_mrm(a01_syn)
class(res)
str(res$summary_lines[c("n", "Treated prevalence")])
ens <- as_table(res$tables[[1]])
ens[, c("Estimator", "Estimand", "Estimate", "SE", "95% CI")]
```

The second table compares four standard errors for the IRM-DML
estimate: pooled, clustered on fiscal year, clustered on person, and
two-way:

```{r multi-se}
as_table(res$tables[[2]])[, c("SE flavour", "ATE", "SE", "95% CI")]
```

The third table is a sensitivity arm built by
`morie_otis_make_pair_alert_to_volatility_naive()`: the treatment is
"at least two alert flags at once in some row of the person-year", and
the outcome is binary (any row whose two region columns differ):

```{r naive}
as_table(res$tables[[3]])[, c("Estimator", "ATE", "SE", "95% CI")]
```

The individual estimator outputs are kept in `res$payload$ensemble`.

# The general multi-estimator entry point

`morie_mrm_estimate_causal_effect()` takes any data frame with a
binary treatment and runs up to four estimators (nearest-neighbour
matching, IPW, AIPW and DML) on the same specification. It adjusts the
p-values for multiple testing (Holm by default) and pools the
estimates. `morie_mrm_report()` renders the result:

```{r mrm-effect}
eff <- morie_mrm_estimate_causal_effect(
  pair$data, treatment = pair$T, outcome = pair$Y,
  covariates = pair$covariates,
  methods = c("matching", "ate", "aipw", "dml"),
  correction = "holm"
)
cat(morie_mrm_report(eff, format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
```

For a single estimator, `morie_estimate_ate()` returns one Hajek IPW
estimate with its standard error and confidence interval, and
`morie_estimate_aipw()` one augmented IPW estimate:

```{r single}
ipw <- morie_estimate_ate(pair$data, pair$T, pair$Y, pair$covariates)
unlist(ipw[c("ate", "se", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "n", "ess")])
```

# Aggregate companion: incidence-rate ratios

`morie_otis_irr_glmm_vm()` builds person-year cells from table b01 with
the same builder as the a01 design
(`morie_otis_make_pair_alert_to_volatility_ruhela()`) and fits Poisson and
negative-binomial GLMs of the regional-volatility count `Y_vm_count` (region
changes) on `T_high_ac` (alert-state complexity of at least 2), adjusting
for year, gender and age band. It has no random effect and no cluster-robust standard error,
and says so in its warnings. On the 1,000-row b01 extract, few
person-years are treated, so the interval is wide:

```{r irr}
irr <- morie_otis_irr_glmm_vm(b01)
irr
```

# Mandela classification

Rule 44 of the UN Mandela Rules defines solitary confinement as
confinement for 22 hours or more a day without meaningful human
contact, and prolonged solitary confinement as solitary confinement
for more than 15 consecutive days; Rule 43 prohibits prolonged
solitary confinement.

`morie_otis_analyze_c11_mandela_classification()` applies the 15-day
threshold to OTIS table c11 (individuals by aggregate length of
confinement). OTIS records no hours out of cell, so the provincial
classification is a duration-only proxy:

```{r c11}
c11 <- morie_sample("otis_c11")
m11 <- morie_otis_analyze_c11_mandela_classification(c11)
as_table(m11$tables[[1]])
```

`morie_otis_analyze_otis_mandela_provincial_vs_federal()` sets those
rates beside the federal Structured Intervention Unit figures of
Sprott and Doob (2021, Table 19):

```{r prov-fed}
pf <- morie_otis_analyze_otis_mandela_provincial_vs_federal(c11)
as_table(pf$tables[[1]])
```

The units differ (federal person-stays, provincial individuals), as
the function's caveat line states.

Three further classifiers work on single records:

```{r classifiers}
# Federal SIU stay: days, average hours out of cell, % of days missing 4 h
morie_siu_classify_mandela(20, 1.5, 100)$category
# OTIS alert flags (mental health, suicide risk, suicide watch) + duration
morie_otis_classify_mandela_combo(1, 1, 0, days = 20)$mandela_category
# Placement-level rates on b01
mrm_classify_mandela(b01, denominator = "row")
```

`morie_otis_analyze_b05_mandela_classification()` applies the same
threshold to table b05 (placements by consecutive length). b05 is not
in the catalogue, so read it straight from data.ontario.ca (network;
not run here):

```{r b05, eval = FALSE}
b05 <- utils::read.csv(paste0(
  "https://data.ontario.ca/dataset/09f7fc65-d3bb-4ca8-8b84-1cdc3ef73c36/",
  "resource/754e8cde-5c74-4c0a-9782-79767a2b26b0/download/",
  "b05_segregation_placements_consecutive_lengths.csv"),
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
m05 <- morie_otis_analyze_b05_mandela_classification(b05)
as_table(m05$tables[[1]])
```

# Federal counterparts

The federal side has its own functions:

- `morie_siuiap_panel_summary()` describes the Structured Intervention
  Unit Implementation Advisory Panel, and `MORIE_SIUIAP_REPORTS` lists
  its reports; `morie_siuiap_cite()` gives the citation of one report.
- `analyze_doob_table1_releases()`,
  `analyze_doob_table2_flow()`,
  `analyze_doob_table3_age_overrepresentation()` and
  `analyze_doob_full_affidavit()` reproduce the tables of Doob's
  Federal Court affidavit from the published CCRSO figures.
- `morie_siu_verify_published_chi_squares()` recomputes five
  published chi-square statistics from the Sprott--Doob and
  Sprott--Doob--Iftene reports.

```{r federal}
names(MORIE_SIUIAP_REPORTS)
morie_siuiap_cite("final_2024")
doob1 <- analyze_doob_table1_releases()
as_table(doob1$tables[[1]])
```
